subtype: Approach: asking a parent to remind him at night [Action]
passage: In the cricket club's changing room, Coach Reena read the list for tomorrow's match: whites, pads, ID card, water bottle. Hemant nodded, but his stomach dropped. Last month he had forgotten his ID card and been kept out of the warm-up. He knew his own head. In the car park, he told his father, "Papa, tonight after dinner, please ask me what I need for tomorrow. Then I'll pack." Papa smiled. "Whites, pads, ID, water," said Hemant. "Ask me." At nine o'clock Papa asked, Hemant listed all four, and zipped the kitbag shut. He was at the gate with everything at eight the next morning.

qa.q: What four things did the coach list for the match?
qa.a: The coach listed whites, pads, ID card and water bottle.

qa.q: Why did Hemant ask his father to remind him?
qa.a: Hemant remembered forgetting the ID card last month and knew his own head, so he felt worried and wanted a helper for this important list. 😰

qa.q: What alternative approach could Hemant use next time, and why?
qa.a: Hemant could keep a written checklist inside the kitbag or pack right after practice. A list does not depend on anyone else being free.

qa.q: How might Papa see Hemant's request?
qa.a: Papa smiled and asked at nine as agreed, so Papa probably feels glad that Hemant took responsibility and asked for help.

grounding: Knowing he tends to forget, a boy asks his father to quiz him in the evening about what he needs, using another person as a memory helper.

subtype: Approach: asking a parent to remind him at night [Action]
passage: My brother Asif forgets things. Everyone in our flat knows it. So I was surprised on Tuesday when he went up to Abbu at dinner, before anyone had nagged him, and said, "Abbu, tomorrow is the science exhibition. Can you ask me at nine o'clock what I need? Ask properly, like a quiz." Abbu raised his eyebrows but said yes. At nine Abbu called from the sofa, "Quiz time. What do you need?" Asif stood very straight. "Model, the signed form, white shirt." He ran to the shelf, found the form still unsigned, and brought it over with a pen. I don't know if he was worried or just trying something new. But in the morning he left with all three.

qa.q: What time did Abbu agree to ask Asif about the exhibition?
qa.a: Abbu agreed to ask at nine o'clock.

qa.q: What might Asif have been feeling when he asked Abbu for help?
qa.a: He may have been worried about forgetting on such an important day, though the observer is not sure; asking early shows he wanted to get it right.

qa.q: What other approach could help Asif on ordinary school days, and why?
qa.a: He could keep a written checklist by the door, because asking Abbu works for one big day but a list helps every day.

qa.q: How does Asif's request look to Abbu?
qa.a: Abbu is surprised, raising his eyebrows, and then willing to play along, probably pleased that Asif asked on his own.

grounding: It shows a boy who knows he forgets asking his father to quiz him in the evening about an important one-time list.

subtype: Approach: asking a parent to remind him at night [Action]
passage:
Monday: Sports Day was on Thursday, and Coach read out the list: white shoes, house T-shirt, ID badge. Sumit knew himself. "I will remember it today and forget it by Wednesday," he thought. At home he asked his father, "Papa, on Wednesday night, will you ask me what I need for Sports Day?" Bhupen nodded and wrote "Ask Sumit" on the calendar.
Wednesday: At eight, Papa tapped the calendar. "What do you need tomorrow?" Sumit named the shoes and T-shirt, then paused. "Badge!" It was still in his winter blazer. He pinned it to the T-shirt.
Thursday: Sumit lined up with his house, badge flashing in the sun.

qa.q: What did Bhupen write on the calendar?
qa.a: He wrote "Ask Sumit" on the calendar.

qa.q: How did Sumit feel when he remembered the badge on Wednesday?
qa.a: He felt a jolt of alarm and then relief, because the question caught the missing badge in time.

qa.q: Which other approach could Sumit add, and why?
qa.a: He could pack the bag right after Papa's question, because answering and packing together leaves nothing to forget in the morning.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Bhupen?
qa.a: Bhupen is happy to be a memory helper for one important day, since it takes only a note and a question.

grounding: It shows a boy who tends to forget asking his father to check in the evening what he needs for an important day.
